speaker: abel_garnish
text: Twenty-four stands. I had it at breakfast and I have it now. A parlour is not a yard. If you have a tune, Master Kemp, the tune can wait until someone has paid to hear it.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I have a scrap, and a scrap is how a song begins. You may hear four notes and keep your pin in your pocket. I am not asking you to love me before dinner.

speaker: will_kemp
text: There was a lass, and she had a pan, and the pan was hotter than the—

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Stop. That is a kitchen. I do not tick kitchens. Bring it to the yard this afternoon, whole, in front of the holiday, and I will say whether it was a song. Until then the book says twenty-four, and twenty-four has no music under it.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Leave him the pin, Will. Thou wilt have the yard soon enough, and a yard of apprentices is a better judge than a tiring-room that wants its breakfast. I am not defending the pin. I am defending the hour.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thou hast the hour right, Dick. The scrap is not the song, and I am not writing either of them down this morning. Twenty-four is the tally until the yard changes it. You may be funny after two. You may not be funny into Abel's margin before it.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: The watchet sits. The voice is where it was on Friday. I am not asking for a new gown for one afternoon, and I am not asking for a new speech. If the Princess comes on, she comes on as she did.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thou wilt do. This afternoon is the last of this bill. Do not spend the voice in the yard before two, and do not invent a line because the holiday is loud. Loud is their business. Clean is thine.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Clean. The boy is clean, the book is clean, and I am to be dirty only when it pays. You are a very Lenten company for a Tuesday. I shall be good until the pancake is in them, and then I shall not be your fault.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: You are already my fault if I tick you early. I will not. Nick, the watchet is brushed. Leave it on the peg until they call the Princess. Master Will, your margin stays at twenty-four. I will bring the book out after, not before.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The third time, and the last before the dark. I am not improving Navarre because it is Shrove. The rhymes I trust are the rhymes they have already bought. Thou wilt leave the last page, Will. We agreed it when the yard surprised thee. The yard may surprise thee again. That is not a reason to rewrite at nine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not rewriting. The ending stands. The tally stands. The song, if it is a song, stands or falls out there, where Abel can hear it without guessing. Nick, if the voice goes thin, thou shortens the line. Thou dost not decorate it.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I will shorten before I decorate. The watchet is a gown, not a trumpet. I know the difference. I knew it on Friday.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Friday was a quiet saint compared with this street. Let him be good. Let me be patient for three hours, which is a miracle you may enter if you like, Abel, though I know you will not enter a miracle. You only enter lines.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: I enter what the yard takes. Miracles are above my pay, and so is a tune sung to a bench. Twenty-four. I will say it once more, so nobody carries eleven in his head from a month ago. Eleven is buried. Twenty-four is the morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twenty-four is the morning. I will not argue a number I have already accepted, and I will not accept a new one until you speak it after the play. Dick, nine has done its work. I am going home to a pancake that is not your concern, and to an almanac.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Go. Thou wilt be back before two, and thou wilt not bring the almanac on with thee. My lord may have the day. The yard has the comedy. I can hold both without a sum of anybody's years.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: No sums of years, and no sums of lines beyond twenty-four, until I have heard the afternoon. If the scrap becomes a song, I will say one song. If it dies in the tiring-room, it died here, and it will not haunt the book.

speaker: will_kemp
text: It will not die. It will wait, which is harder, and I am doing the harder thing so you may all admire me and refuse to write the admiration down. You, boy. Breathe. The gown does the shining. You do the words you already have.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I have them. I am not adding. I will be here at two, and I will not be in the yard at noon practising where the orange-sellers can score me.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good. Two of the clock, the third time, the last time. Abel, shut the margin. Kemp, keep the pan out of this room. I have heard enough of the lass to know she is not in the book yet, and I am content.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Content is not the same as copied. I will bring the book this afternoon shut, and I will open it when the yard has finished, not when anyone is feeling literary in a passage.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then nine has finished its work. Thou wilt eat, Will, and thou wilt be back before two, and thou wilt not bring me a new last page on a trencher.

speaker: nick_sorrell
text: I will be back before two. The watchet stays on the peg until they call. I am not practising where the orange-sellers can score me, and I am not asking what the tune will become.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The tune will be whatever the yard gives back. You may all go and be serious. I shall sit here and be patient, and you may behold the patience and not write it down. Patience is not one of the twenty-four.
